hook: Edward Feigenbaum studied electrical engineering at the Carnegie Institute of Technology, where he also earned his PhD under Herbert Simon, building EPAM, an early computer model of human memory and learning. He joined the faculty at the University of California, Berkeley, in 1960 and moved to Stanford University in 1965, where he spent most of his career and later chaired the computer science department. At Stanford he worked with the geneticist Joshua Lederberg on DENDRAL, a program that inferred the molecular structure of chemical compounds from mass spectrometry data by encoding the reasoning of expert chemists, widely regarded as the first true expert system. Feigenbaum and his colleagues went on to build MYCIN, a program that used a similar rule-based approach to help diagnose bacterial infections and recommend antibiotic treatment, and his work established knowledge engineering, the practice of capturing human expertise as computable rules, as a distinct discipline within artificial intelligence. He directed Stanford's Knowledge Systems Laboratory for many years, served as chief scientist of the United States Air Force from 1994 to 1997, and in 1994 shared the A.M. Turing Award with Raj Reddy for demonstrating the practical and commercial potential of large-scale artificial intelligence systems.

achievements.title: DENDRAL, developed with Joshua Lederberg
achievements.impact: Built one of the first true expert systems, using encoded chemical reasoning to infer molecular structures from mass spectrometry data, and demonstrated that expert-level knowledge could be captured in software.

achievements.title: MYCIN
achievements.impact: Extended the expert-system approach to medicine, helping diagnose bacterial infections and recommend antibiotic therapy, and became an influential model for later medical decision-support systems.

achievements.title: Founding contributions to knowledge engineering
achievements.impact: Established the practice of systematically capturing human expert knowledge as computable rules, shaping how expert systems were built for decades.

achievements.title: A.M. Turing Award, 1994
achievements.impact: Shared with Raj Reddy for pioneering the design and construction of large-scale artificial intelligence systems and demonstrating their practical and commercial value.

achievements.title: EPAM (Elementary Perceiver and Memorizer)
achievements.impact: An early computational model of human verbal learning and memory, developed as part of his doctoral research under Herbert Simon.
